8f6f9667b587: How does Scrooge feel when he sees Dick Wilkins again?
Scrooge says Dick “was very much attached to me” and sighs “Poor Dick! Dear, dear!”, showing warm affection mixed with sadness.
What does Fezziwig's behaviour suggest about him as an employer?
He is generous and cheerful with his workers
He is strict and works them late
He is nervous about losing money
He calls out “No more work to-night” and “Christmas, Ebenezer!” with “a sharp clap of his hands,” giving his apprentices the evening off joyfully.
What is the effect of the counting “one, two, three … seven, eight, nine” in the description of the shutters?
It shows how fast and eager the two young men are
It shows how many shutters were broken
It slows the story down to build fear
It shows the young men are bad at counting
The counting races along until they “came back before you could have got to twelve, panting like race-horses,” stressing their speed and excitement.
268f91825d12: What is Lavinia suggesting when she asks if Sara could pretend as a beggar?
That Sara's imagining is easy only because she is rich
That Sara would make a good actress
That beggars are better at pretending

To show that Miss Amelia was eavesdropping
To explain why the feast was cancelled

01ca5994e7ec: What does the word “shouldered” suggest about how Stryver treats Mr. Lorry?
Stryver pushes him aside rudely and selfishly
Stryver supports him like a friend

He is self-important and unconcerned with others' tiredness

To use her concern for her father to end the meeting
To ask her permission to leave alone

3126089c3dc2: What is Wollstonecraft's main objection to the advice she quotes?

It gives women too much power over men

What does the image “kiss the rod” most nearly mean here?
Accept punishment meekly instead of resisting
Fall in love with a cruel person
Celebrate a victory over an enemy
The heart that will “kiss the rod” is one that, “instead of revolting at injustice,” submits to it.
Why does she call such behaviour “mere expedients”?
They are short-term tricks, not true virtue
They are laws passed by government
They are the natural duties of women
She says “expedients are only useful for the moment,” meaning tactics of softness do not build real, lasting virtue.
8f5c71d38fdd: Why does the Pigeon think Alice is a serpent?
It only cares that she might steal its eggs
She is hissing at the Pigeon
She is hiding in the grass
She told the Pigeon she was one

What does the word “sulky” tell us about the Pigeon?

What does Alice's careful nibbling of the mushroom show about her?
She has learned how to control her size
She is very hungry after her walk
She wants to grow as tall as possible
She is trying to poison the Pigeon

7d6e370bccb4: Why can't the animals decide whether life is better than before?
They have no memories or records except Squealer's figures
They are too happy to care
Jones has returned to the farm

They show that life is getting worse

He cannot remember anything at all

12cd7e1b2b2e: Why does Marilla tell Anne to give Davy jam on his bread?
She guesses he had a poor tea at the Boulters'

What changes Davy's mood partway through his speech?

“Davy brightened up as the insidious comfort of the plum jam stole into his soul,” and he ends with “This jam is awful nice.”
1668a448a875: Why does Marilla warn Anne to be careful how she behaves?
Mrs. Barry only lets Diana play with good children

f6565eede632: What is the main purpose of the long description of the sledge?
To help readers picture an unusual vehicle
To show that Mr. Fogg is an engineer
To explain why the train broke down

d3e9f4609265: What does the simile comparing the aunt and children to “a housefly that refuses to be discouraged” suggest?
Their talk is constant and irritating
Their talk is quiet and soothing

bb9b105e0a30: What kind of place are the horses taken to?

8c16055c1d86: What is Paine's main claim in this passage?

2e0566c7382c: How does the narrator's mood shift across the passage?

6d43f8385a1d: What does the phrase “this was seeing life, at least” suggest about Jimmy?
